messages:
jen_support: heads up — WidgetCo (tenant: widgetco-prod) reporting missing spans in Trace View for v1 checkout. Their logs contain the request_id but console trace view shows no spans. Sample request id: req-9a8b7c6d. Started ~03:00 UTC. They attached screenshots and say 'no spans found' when searching that req id. Can someone triage? cc @tom_oncall @aya_ingest

tom_oncall: looking. any ingestion errors or failed batches at that time? did they recently update the agent or proxy in front of their services?

jen_support: reproducer from support: we replayed a POST to /v1/ingest/trace with header `X-Request-Id: req-9a8b7c6d` and got 202. but console still doesn't link the request to traces. customer says their frontend proxy might rewrite headers (they suspect `X-Request-Id` -> `X-Req-Id`). sample headers they sent: `X-Request-Id: req-9a8b7c6d`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.

aya_ingest: quick check in ES: I can see spans around that time but parent references are null for a bunch. Query I ran: `GET /traces/_search?q=request_id:req-9a8b7c6d` — returns a few spans but several entries have request_id variants like `req=9a8b7c6d` and `req_9a8b7c6d`. looks like header normalization happened somewhere.

marco_frontend: we rolled nginx v1.22 last week. nginx has `underscores_in_headers` and other header normalization knobs but we don't touch dashes. however I did spot a custom lua filter on the proxy that runs `string.gsub(header, "-", "=")` for legacy reasons 😬. investigating now.

tom_oncall: can you paste the raw request (headers + small payload) that reproduces it? also note we shipped request_id salting in router (salt v2) last Wednesday — if some components used unsalted vs salted forms that could break stitching.

liu_srebot: ingest-alert: spike detected for orphaned_spans for tenant widgetco-prod at 2026-02-10T03:12Z (+480% vs baseline). Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/ingest/orphaned-spans?tenant=widgetco-prod&range=1h

aya_ingest: found something: some spans in ES show request_id stored as `req=9a8b7c6d` (equals sign) and others as base64 like `cjktOWE4YjdjNmQ=` — looks like client or proxy sometimes URL-encodes or base64-encodes the header. running a script to enumerate variants and backfill links.

jen_support: customer notes they set request id in the browser via `fetch()` using `headers.set('X-Request-Id', id)`. their frontend uses `credentials: 'include'`. could CORS preflight or our proxy be dropping/altering the header for that origin?

marco_frontend: CORS can block custom headers unless `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` includes them. we added `X-Request-Id` to allowed headers generally, but the proxy lua filter that I mentioned also runs only for widgetco-prod origin — that filter is likely mangling the header when the preflight path is taken. reverting the filter for that origin now.

aya_ingest: mitigation plan: add tolerant stitching in the ingest pipeline that canonicalizes incoming request ids (normalize separators, try base64->raw, strip non-alphanum) so small mangles don't produce orphaned spans. I'm preparing a canary patch to roll to 10% of ingest nodes. will also add a diagnostic that emits 'candidate_request_ids' to console UI when exact match fails.

tom_oncall: approve the canary for tolerant stitching. also let's add a short-term backfill job to link existing orphan spans for widgetco-prod using the enumerated variants. postmortem should cover router salt versioning and the proxy lua change.

jen_support: customer confirmed new traffic shows linked spans after we reverted the proxy filter. they're happy for now but request RCA and timeline. I'll escalate to their AE and send an interim summary. thanks all :thumbsup:

aya_ingest: RCA summary (will convert to full postmortem): root cause = proxy header mangling (lua filter) + missing CORS header in one edge case which caused client to re-encode header; symptoms = orphaned spans / request_id variants (`-` -> `=`, underscore/dash swaps, base64 variants); mitigations = revert proxy filter, ingest tolerant stitching (canary -> rollout), console diagnostic for candidate ids, backfill for affected window. action items: 1) patch ingest pipeline (AYA), 2) add console candidate ids (ENG-UI), 3) update docs & agent guidance (DOCS), 4) follow up with WidgetCo about their fetch usage.

jen_support: I'll post an incident summary to #incidents and notify widgetco's account team. closing this thread but will follow up with postmortem link.
